questions.question: Why is mains electricity dangerous, and why does water make it worse?
questions.expected_answer: Mains electricity pushes much harder than a cell and can cause electric shocks, burns and fires, and it can kill. Water conducts electricity, so wet hands or wet floors make it easier for electricity to flow through a person.

questions.question: Give four safety rules for using electricity at home.
questions.expected_answer: Any four: use switches and plugs only with dry hands; never use appliances near baths or basins; never push anything except a plug into a plug point; unplug a toaster before removing stuck bread; do not overload multiplugs; do not use damaged cords; pull plugs out by the plug, not the cord; let only qualified electricians do repairs.

questions.question: Give three safety rules outdoors, and explain how to help someone who is getting an electric shock.
questions.expected_answer: Never climb pylons or trees near power lines; never fly kites near lines; stay away from substations and fallen power lines; never touch loose wires or illegal connections. To help, do not touch the person; switch off the power if it is safe, or push them away from the wire with something dry and non-metal, like a wooden broom handle, then call 10177 or 112.
